cohort: Children aged 3-12 years in Quito, Ecuador
finding: Children delivered via cesarean section had a higher risk of wheezing, physician-diagnosed asthma, and atopic dermatitis compared to those delivered vaginally, with the association only significant in children of medium/high socioeconomic backgrounds.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of allergic disorders, including asthma and dermatitis.
